data.content_ref: inline:The target's own mechanism contains an internal contradiction that undermines its dissolution. The claim proposes an evolutionary selection mechanism where rationality emerges from population-level dynamics of theory selection, and the mechanism section concludes: 'It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all.' This conclusion is a non-sequitur that contradicts the dissolution's own premises. An evolutionary selection process requires differential fitness: some theories survive because they possess structural properties (corroboration, falsifiability, empirical adequacy) that make them fitter than rivals. If the underlying structure of theories were 'never relevant,' there would be no selection gradient—only random drift—and the emergent 'rationality' the target invokes would be indistinguishable from noise. The target cannot simultaneously claim (a) that rationality emerges from a selection mechanism that preferentially retains better theories and (b) that the structure distinguishing better from worse theories is irrelevant to the outcome. The selection mechanism the target invokes is parasitic on the very inductive or structural considerations it claims to render irrelevant. Prior objections targeted the individual-vs-systemic justification gap; this objection targets the logical incoherence of the dissolution's own mechanism: the evolutionary analogy only works if theory structure matters, which the mechanism explicitly denies.
